title: Renewal & expansion check-in - GreenBox Logistics
next_steps: Samir to send updated 3-region dedicated pricing and contract amendment by 2027-03-11
Elena to share latency/cost benchmark spreadsheet and proposed batching profile by 2027-03-12
Michael to confirm target go-live window for additional EU region (end of Q2) by 2027-03-16
Jordan to schedule technical POC run (1 day benchmark) w/ GreenBox infra team for week of 2027-03-21
action_items: Samir Patel: prepare contract amendment draft for 12-month extension + 3-region dedicated commit - due 2027-03-11
Elena Kwon: run and share bench results for 5k rps simulated load and cost per 1k tokens across regions - due 2027-03-12
Michael Chen: confirm data residency requirements for EU and APAC regions - due 2027-03-16
summary: Renewal check-in focused on capacity upgrade and adding EU region. Customer is leaning toward Dedicated reserved capacity for predictability and data isolation; also discussed contract extension and pilot benchmarks. Action items for pricing, benchmarks, and scheduling a POC.
transcript:
[00:00] Samir Patel: Hey everybody, thanks for hopping on, appreciate you all making time. quick agenda: renewal, capacity options, regions, and any blockers for extending the contract.
[00:12] Tom Baker: Yeah thanks Samir, we got about 45 minutes here. Rita and Michael are on from infra and ML.
[00:18] Michael Chen: Hey all. Quick note - we saw token costs creep up last quarter and some tail latency on larger inference batches. want to understand dedicated options.
[00:30] Elena Kwon: Totally, Michael. For context we looked at your recent usage - mostly steady traffic w/ periodic spikes during end-of-day shipments. Dedicated will give you predictable throughput and isolation, we can also pin model versions.
[00:45] Rita Alvarez: The big ask from infra is EU region support and KMS integration for keys, plus SOC2 audit artifacts.
[00:52] Samir Patel: Yep. On the contract front you’re up for renewal in May - you mentioned wanting a 12-month extension and exploring reserved capacity across NA + EU?
[01:05] Michael Chen: Correct. Also curious about adding APAC later, but immediate priority is EU. latency from EU users is a concern.
[01:18] Elena Kwon: For latency, we recommend a 3-region dedicated pool - NA, EU, APAC-ready - where APAC can be cold-standby until you want it live. That gets median latency down and provides failover.
[01:32] Tom Baker: How does pricing change for multi-region? Our procurement team will need clear delta for the extension.
[01:38] Samir Patel: Great question. The delta is primarily reserved GPU capacity + inter-region egress. I'll send a tailored pricing sheet but roughly it's an uplift of ~35% for an extra region with committed throughput.
[01:52] Michael Chen: 35% - okay. Is there a way to trade cost for latency? like lower-cost quantization or different batching to keep within budget?
[02:05] Elena Kwon: Yes; we can use quantized model variants and intelligent batching profiles. There's a tradeoff: 4-bit quantization can reduce footprint and cost but may impact quality a bit on some prompts. We can run a short eval suite with your prompts.
[02:25] Rita Alvarez: On compliance: we need KMS/HSM support and detailed audit logs. we heard Redwood has a private deployment option - is that what we need?
[02:36] Samir Patel: Private is an option, but for most customers Dedicated with KMS integration and VPC peering meets requirements. Private/on-prem is for air-gapped or very strict regulated cases. For GreenBox, Dedicated + KMS + audit logs likely fits.
[02:55] Michael Chen: Great. Can you confirm log retention windows and SSO options?
[03:00] Elena Kwon: We support SAML SSO, RBAC, and customizable retention - typical retention packages are 90 days standard, can be extended as an add-on. We'll put specifics in the security packet.
[03:12] Tom Baker: Procurement will want a contract amendment with the extension term + regional add-on defined. Who will draft it?
[03:18] Samir Patel: We'll draft the amendment. I'll include the committed throughput, region definitions, and SLA adjustments.
[03:25] Michael Chen: On benchmark/POC: we'd like a 1-day benchmark simulating peak end-of-day -- roughly 5k RPS of inference calls with typical payloads. can Redwood run that in our staging?
[03:38] Elena Kwon: Absolutely. We can run a POC on Dedicated pre-provisioned GPUs; we'll need a list of typical prompts, token distributions, and any whitelisting details for IPs.
[03:50] Rita Alvarez: We'll also need to validate egress costs and any cross-region replication effects.
[03:55] Elena Kwon: We'll include estimated egress numbers in the benchmark spreadsheet.
[04:00] Jordan Lee: Quick note - from CSM side I’ll coordinate scheduling and make sure previous support tickets are closed before the POC.
[04:08] Michael Chen: Awesome. Another question: fallback behaviors if a region loses capacity - automatic routing to another region?
[04:16] Elena Kwon: Yes, smart routing can failover to a compatible model variant in another region; you can set policies to prefer latency or cost. If you prefer cost, it'll route to lower-cost variant; for latency it biases nearest region.
[04:30] Tom Baker: Any dependencies on our side for network or infra to enable regional Dedicated?
[04:36] Samir Patel: We'll need VPC peering, a few firewall rules for control plane connectivity, and KMS configuration. We'll provide a runbook.
[04:46] Michael Chen: For model versions: we want to pin to the v2.1 checkpoint that showed best UAT results. Can Dedicated pin model versions?
[04:54] Elena Kwon: Yes, you can pin model versions and roll out canary patches. Also we support automatic fallback to an older checkpoint during rollouts.
[05:06] Rita Alvarez: What's the SLA for Dedicated across regions? uptime and latency SLOs?
[05:12] Samir Patel: We have SLA tiers. For reserved Dedicated we commit to 99.9% uptime and latency targets per model/route; details vary by commit size - we'll attach the SLA appendix.
[05:25] Michael Chen: Sounds good. One risk - the quantized model caused hallucination on a small set of prompts last time. We need quality regression alerts tied to our eval set.
[05:36] Elena Kwon: We can wire quality monitoring and regression alerts to be driven by your prompt set; Redwood Optimize will monitor drift and trigger alerts if metrics fall beyond thresholds.
[05:50] Tom Baker: Procurement timeline: we need final pricing and contract by March 11 to sign before current renewal window. Is that doable?
[05:58] Samir Patel: Yes, we can aim for that. Elena will run bench and I’ll send pricing; Jordan will coordinate.
[06:05] Michael Chen: Regarding APAC cold-standby - how quickly can you bring it online?
[06:09] Elena Kwon: If pre-provisioned as a hot standby, minutes; if cold-standby, a few hours depending on model load and kv-cache warmup. There is a cost delta for hot standby.
[06:20] Rita Alvarez: We'll likely keep APAC cold for now and flip on later.
[06:24] Samir Patel: Noted. OK let's walk through next steps - Samir will draft contract amendment, Elena will run benchmarks and share spreadsheet, Jordan schedules POC.
[06:36] Tom Baker: Great - please include an itemized egress estimate and the contract language around region addition.
[06:42] Samir Patel: Will do. Any other asks?
[06:46] Michael Chen: Do you have any migration downtime expected for the move to Dedicated?
[06:51] Elena Kwon: Minimal - we can gradually redirect traffic and use canary routes to avoid downtime. There may be a short window for KV-cache warmups if switching variants.
[07:05] Rita Alvarez: Ok thanks everyone.
[07:08] Samir Patel: Thanks all. Recap - pricing and amendment by 3/11, bench by 3/12, POC week of 3/21, Michael to confirm EU requirements by 3/16.
[07:20] Jordan Lee: I'll follow up with calendar invites.
[07:25] Tom Baker: Thanks, bye.
[07:27] End of recording

Notes: transcription imperfect - some product names transcribed as 'Redwood Opt' or 'red wood dedicate' in places; speaker turns occasionally merged.
